questions.q: What does adding `paths-ignore: ["**.md"]` to a push trigger do?
options: Skips running the workflow when the push only changes Markdown files
Has no effect unless combined with workflow_dispatch
Deletes all Markdown files from the repository on every push
Forces the workflow to run only on Markdown file changes
questions.explain: paths-ignore excludes matching file changes from triggering the workflow, so a docs-only push doesn't kick off a full CI run.

questions.q: On a `pull_request` trigger, what does the `types` field control?
options: Whether the workflow can be triggered manually
Which programming language the job uses
Which pull request sub-events (like opened or synchronize) actually trigger the workflow
The runner operating system
questions.explain: types narrows a pull_request trigger to specific sub-events; opened, synchronize, and reopened are the default if types is omitted.

questions.q: What timezone does GitHub Actions use for `schedule` cron expressions?
options: The runner's local timezone, which varies by region
The repository owner's profile timezone
UTC, always
Eastern Time, regardless of where the repository is hosted
questions.explain: Scheduled workflows always evaluate cron expressions in UTC, regardless of where the repository or its contributors are located.

questions.q: What does `workflow_dispatch` add to a repository?
options: A required approval step before any push can merge
An automatic nightly run with no way to trigger it manually
A way to delete old workflow runs
A manual "Run workflow" button in the Actions tab, optionally with input fields
questions.explain: workflow_dispatch lets someone trigger the workflow by hand from the Actions tab; its optional inputs block adds a small form for that run.
